item.title: Kashima Jingu: An Ancient Shrine of Martial Arts & Deer — Guide
item.description: Kashima Jingu, with a history said to stretch back over 2,600 years, is one of Japan’s oldest and most revered shrines, historically associated with the deity of martial arts and long considered the spiritual birthplace of Japanese swordsmanship, with several historic dojos in the surrounding area still tracing their lineage to the shrine. Beyond the vermillion main gate, a dense sacred forest path leads past a small deer park (deer being messengers of the shrine’s deity) to an inner shrine and a mysterious ‘rock that binds earthquakes,’ with the shrine’s grand autumn festival drawing large crowds each September.

item.title: Okinawa Karate Guide: The Birthplace, Dojos & Experiences
item.description: Okinawa is the birthplace of karate, which grew from the indigenous Ryukyu fighting art “te” blended with Chinese martial influences. For practitioners worldwide, training in Okinawa is a pilgrimage to the source; for travellers, it’s a rare chance to step into a traditional dojo and learn the basics — stances, blocks, strikes and the spirit of respect at the heart of the art. With beginner-friendly experiences and the impressive Okinawa Karate Kaikan, anyone can connect with this living heritage.

item.title: Osaka Kendo Class Guide: Try the Way of the Sword
item.description: Behind the thunderous shouts and clashing bamboo of a dojo lies kendo — “the way of the sword,” the modern martial art descended from samurai swordsmanship. A kendo experience class in Osaka lets visitors step onto the dojo floor, grip the bamboo shinai, learn a few basic cuts and stances, and even try on a piece of the armour, all under an instructor who explains the discipline, spirit, and etiquette behind it.
